newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 5.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.

- The opposition coalition of Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats are poised for victory in Friday's election, with a new opinion poll predicting a 49 percent combined share of the vote for the two parties.
- Prime Minister John Bruton saved his best performance of the three-week election campaign for a television debate with challenger Bertie Ahern on Wednesday.
- A weaker sterling helped the Irish pound climb above 0.91 stg on Wednesday.

- The chairman of British diesel engineering firm Gardner has confirmed his company examined the possibility of buying Belfast-based firm Mackie International earlier this year and is considering making another bid.
- A number of new promises are being made to voters by Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats on the eve of polling, drawing accusations of auction politics.
- Prime Minister John Bruton put in the best performance of his political life in a pre-election television debate on Wednesday, leaving challenger Bertie Ahern for dead.
- The Irish pound has regained some ground against sterling but economists said increases in interest rates are still possible.

- The election remains balanced on a knife-edge after an honours-even debate between John Bruton and Bertie Ahern. - An increase in credit growth figures, particularly home loans, could put further upward pressure on Irish interest rates.
